item.title: Host-Agnostic Static TiddlyWiki Plugin Library
item.content:encoded:
I have updated the architecture of my TiddlyWiki plugin library to support fully static hosting platforms like GitHub Pages, removing the dependency on server-specific backend endpoints.

Up until now, the plugin library typically relied on Tiddlyhost's JSON endpoints to serve plugin data. This new approach allows a plugin library to run anywhere (GitHub Pages, Tiddlyhost, etc) while maintaining full compatibility with any parent TiddlyWiki instance.

Key Technical Changes

- Host-Agnostic via postMessage: Communication between the parent wiki and the library iframe uses a secure window.postMessage bridge, allowing the library to be hosted statically without server-side routing. - Startup Modules (module-type: startup): The library now uses a native TiddlyWiki startup module instead of manual script injection in the HTML head, ensuring clean execution timing during the boot sequence. - In-Memory Retrieval: When a user requests a plugin, the library extracts the tiddler directly from the local in-memory store using $tw.wiki.getTiddler(), avoiding secondary network roundtrips. - Native JavaScript Compilation: Metadata, readmes, and icons are processed and serialized in JavaScript. This replaces the previous wikitext macro approach, preventing parsing errors from unescaped quotes or missing SVG namespaces.

Links

You can view the updated implementation and live library at: 👉 https://plugins.theophile.dev

This approach will soon replace the current method used in this plugin library.

item.title: RSS Feed Plugin 0.0.4: Added auto upload feature
item.content:encoded: The RSS Feed plugin now has a Background Actions that check when a tiddler is added or removed from the feed and automatically send the update to github. Note that modifications done to a tiddler are not detected, so if you want to update the feed after editing a tiddler, remember to manually send the feed to github using the button, or let the plugin update the feed when a new tiddler is added or removed from the feed. This feature can be disabled in the plugin settings.

item.title: Announcing the RSS Feed Plugin
item.content:encoded: I am excited to announce the release of a new plugin designed to allow your audience to follow your wiki. This new tool automatically generates a valid RSS 2.0 feed directly from your specified tiddlers and pushes the file from your wiki, straight to GitHub.
